summary: This diff adds a new file, skills/p-review/SKILL.md, defining a 'p-review' skill for fast, single-reviewer adversarial review of an existing artifact (plan, spec, or diff). The conductor gathers artifact/baseline/intent, dispatches a fresh subagent with a fixed reviewer brief, rules on findings (rejecting only false-premise ones), then presents Concerns, Noted-not-recommended, Rejected, and a Minor list written to a separate file for a downstream auto-fix agent. An --inline flag skips the subagent and rules step for a faster single-pass review.

claims.text: Frontmatter defines name 'p-review' and a description covering when to use vs. not use it
Baseline ref is resolved via `git merge-base HEAD @{u}`, falling back to `git merge-base HEAD "$(git symbolic-ref --short refs/remotes/origin/HEAD)"`, and asking the user if that also fails
The conductor always dispatches a fresh subagent as Reviewer, even under conditions where the artifact isn't the conductor's own
Under --inline, the dispatch and Ruling step are both skipped and the conductor follows the brief itself
The reviewer brief instructs the subagent not to surface issues a compiler/type-checker/linter/test run would already catch
Findings are split into Concerns (need user judgment, ranked /10) and Minor (for a downstream auto-fix agent, no decision needed)
The Ruling step lets the conductor veto a finding only if it rests on a misunderstanding or false premise, not to defend the work
The Minor list is written verbatim to minor-findings.md beside the artifact (or repo root if none) and is not summarized or printed to the user

risks.anchor: skills/p-review/SKILL.md:14 ("Do NOT use ... debate-review, adversarial-review, and adversarial-review-2")
risks.note: Explicitly names three other overlapping review skills already in the repo (debate-review, adversarial-review, adversarial-review-2), suggesting this new skill sits close to existing functionality; differentiation rests solely on being 'the cheap one-reviewer pass.'

The baseline-resolution fallback chain has a third failure mode ("That fallback fails too when the clone never set origin/HEAD") which is handled by asking the user rather than a further automated fallback — reasonable, but leaves no automated resolution path documented beyond that point.

least_confident: Whether the described interaction pattern (conductor dispatches subagent, then separately performs a 'Ruling' pass over its findings) is actually implementable as specified within the Agent tool conventions is not verifiable from this chunk alone, since it's a prose/process spec rather than code with visible execution semantics.
